active.title: Kendo Class at Kodokan Budokan
active.description: Step onto the polished floor of the Kodokan — the global home of judo — and take a beginner's session in a martial art practiced here since 1882.
active.bonus: Bow correctly every single time you enter and exit the mat — don't let a sensei have to remind you twice.

active.title: Bouldering at B-PUMP Ogikubo
active.description: Tokyo's climbing culture is fierce and technical — B-PUMP draws serious locals to one of the city's best bouldering walls, where the problem-setting is world class.
active.bonus: Ask the strongest person in the room to set you a project route — attempt it until your forearms give out.

active.title: Cycle the Tamagawa Cycling Road
active.description: Rent a road bike and follow the Tama River 20km from Futako-Tamagawa to the coast — Tokyo peels away and becomes something genuinely wild.
active.bonus: Ride all the way to Tokyo Bay, touch the water, then turn back — no shortcuts.

active.title: Dawn Run Along the Imperial Palace Outer Gardens
active.description: Tokyo's power runners circle the 5km Imperial Palace loop at sunrise — join them and feel the city's quiet ambition before the trains fill.
active.bonus: Run the full loop twice without stopping — nod to every runner you pass.

social.title: Jazz Night at Shinjuku Pit Inn
social.description: Open since 1965, Pit Inn is Tokyo's most serious jazz room — a basement box where world-class musicians play two feet from your face.
social.bonus: Talk to the person next to you between sets — ask them their favorite record and actually listen.

social.title: Sumo Morning Practice at Tomozuna Stable
social.description: Watch elite rikishi train in total silence at a real sumo stable in Ryogoku — an hour of controlled violence and ritual that no museum can replicate.
social.bonus: Bow respectfully at the entrance, stay completely silent, and make eye contact with a wrestler — hold it without flinching.

social.title: Bar Hop Through Golden Gai, Shinjuku
social.description: Six narrow alleys packed with 200 six-seat bars — each one a different world, a different owner, a different reason to stay for one more drink.
social.bonus: Walk in alone to a bar where you're the only foreigner and start a conversation without using your phone as a crutch.

social.title: Karaoke Private Box at Shidax, Shibuya
social.description: Book a private room at Shidax, order unlimited drinks, and discover which song you were actually born to perform.
social.bonus: Sing one song in a language you don't speak — full commitment, no laughing until it's over.

chill.title: Sunrise at Senso-ji Before the Crowds
chill.description: Arrive at Asakusa's 1,400-year-old temple at 6am and you get incense smoke, orange lantern light, and almost no one — a version of Tokyo most visitors never see.
chill.bonus: Draw an omikuji fortune slip — if it's bad luck (kyō), tie it to the rack and walk away without looking back.

chill.title: Onsen Soak at Thermae-Yu, Shinjuku
chill.description: A genuine hot-spring bathhouse in the heart of Shinjuku pulls real sodium bicarbonate water from 1,700 meters below — the silk-water feeling is addictive.
chill.bonus: Try the outdoor rotenburo even in winter — stay until your shoulders are completely loose.

chill.title: Golden Hour at Shinjuku Gyoen
chill.description: Tokyo's finest garden spreads 58 acres of French, English, and Japanese landscapes just minutes from Shinjuku's neon chaos — the contrast is the whole point.
chill.bonus: Find the largest plane tree in the French garden and sit with your back against it for ten full, silent minutes.

chill.title: Afternoon Tea at Kagizen Yoshifusa, Gion-style in Yanaka
chill.description: Yanaka's old-town streets hide Kayaba Coffee, a 1938 kissaten where time genuinely stops over egg salad sandwiches and hand-drip coffee.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your bag for the entire visit — observe the room instead.

foodie.title: Depachika Deep Dive at Isetan Shinjuku B2
foodie.description: The basement food hall of Isetan Shinjuku is Tokyo's most dazzling cathedral of food — every artisan confection, pickled thing, and lacquered bento has earned its place.
foodie.bonus: Spend exactly ¥1,000 and make it count — one item, best possible choice, no hesitation.

foodie.title: Tonkatsu Lunch at Maisen, Omotesando
foodie.description: A converted bathhouse in Omotesando serves Tokyo's most iconic tonkatsu — the kurobuta pork is impossibly tender inside a shard-crisp panko shell.
foodie.bonus: Grind your own sesame seeds in the stone mortar at the table before mixing your sauce — don't let anyone help you.

foodie.title: Omakase Sushi at Sushi Saito
foodie.description: One of the hardest reservations on earth delivers nigiri so precise and seasonal it feels less like dinner and more like a private audience with perfection.
foodie.bonus: Ask Saito-san which piece he is most proud of today — then eat it last.

foodie.title: Ramen at Fuunji, Shinjuku
foodie.description: Fuunji's tsukemen — thick noodles dragged through an intensely rich, chicken-based dipping broth — is the kind of bowl that ruins all other ramen for you.
foodie.bonus: Order the largest portion (tokumori) and finish every drop of broth — ask for the hot dashi to thin it at the end, like a regular.

adventure.title: Tokyo Drift at Odaiba Go-Kart
adventure.description: Strap into a street-legal go-kart dressed as your favorite character and blast through Odaiba's waterfront streets with Rainbow Bridge as your backdrop.
adventure.bonus: Pick the most embarrassing costume available — bonus spark if it's a vegetable.

adventure.title: Roof Scramble at Takao-san via Inariyama Trail
adventure.description: Tokyo's most beloved mountain delivers a ridge-line forest trail, tengu statues, and a skyline payoff that makes you forget the city exists.
adventure.bonus: Ask a stranger at the summit to point out Mount Fuji — then buy them a cup of amazake from the stall.

adventure.title: Night Kayak on the Sumida River
adventure.description: Paddle past illuminated bridges and the Asahi Flame Building on a guided night kayak through old Edo's main waterway.
adventure.bonus: Dip your hand in the Sumida and make a wish — then look up the river's transformation from open sewer to this.

adventure.title: Scramble at Shibuya Crossing
adventure.description: Stand at the center of the world's busiest intersection and let 3,000 people swirl around you like a human tide.
adventure.bonus: Stop dead center when the light changes and hold perfectly still while the crowd parts around you.
